For many, that is a rhetorical question; the Filipino electorate knows the answer. But those who think they are God’s gifts to the Filipino people can never care less for rhetorical questions. Loren Legarda’s website is a superlative spotlight on what a gift she is to the nation—the planet rather. Loren Legarda’s life mantra has been for the Filipino people, the country, and the planet. She is a true Filipina at heart, passionately advocating for the protection of the rights of indigenous peoples and promoting arts and culture in the local and international arena. She started out in the public mind as a reporter of Radio Philippines Network (RPN) during the Marcos dictatorship. A later plum post came at ABS CBN where she was hired as co-anchor of The World Tonight newscast with Angelo Castro Jr. The network would later upgrade her as host of her own current events series The Inside Story. Her journalism career brought her accolades: the Gawad Cultural Center of the Philippines, the Catholic Mass Media Awards Hall of Fame, the Golden Dove Award of the Kapisanan ng mga Brodkasters sa Pilipinas, the Benigno Aquino Award for Journalism, and more than 30 other awards. The verdict was: her name recall was indubitable. That jumpstarted the political career of this “true Filipina at heart” in 1998 when she ran for senator under the Lakas-NUCD-UMDP party. Her presidential candidate was Jose de Venecia. She was the topnotcher of that senatorial race with 15 million votes. Nothing wrong with that. text.preview: The arrest of former speaker Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez inside the Cardinal Santos Hospital in San Juan city last week was, of course, the result of his own cousin's SONA exposing, among others, the alleged flood-control anomalies and many allied charges. That was a landmark event in the country’s history of the administration of justice. Never before in Philippine history has a former speaker of the House been charged and arrested upon the clearance of the president who happens to be his first-degree cousin. It has not been an easy move on the part of president BBM who is not known to be a violent or vengeful man but a compassionate and kind-hearted person. Not many expected that Romualdez would be charged with plunder, which is a non-bailable offense, aside from direct and indirect bribery and money laundering. That means that after his medical issues are properly addressed, he will be brought to the Quezon City detention center in Payatas to join the others, Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta, The arrest of Romualdez and his co-accused was based on the allegations that the former speaker allegedly received kickbacks and commissions on at least 15 occasions between 2022 and 2025. Prosecutors state he imposed a ?2 billion monthly quota on collections. The money was allegedly laundered through shell companies like Golden Pheasant Holdings, Bravos Holdings, and Valiant Consolidated Resource Ferdinand Martin Romualdez, born on November 14, 1963, is the third child of Madam Imelda Marcos' favorite brother Benjamin Kokoy Romualdez, former governor of Leyte and ambassador to the U.S. He is a graduate of UP Law, and Cornell and Harvard universities. He became a lawyer in 1993. He is married to Yedda Marie Mendoza Kittilstvedt who is also an incumbent member of Congress along with his son. Another son is a councilor of Tacloban. output.description: Inilipat na sa New Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory sa Payatas si dating House Speaker Martin Romualdez.
output.text: MANILA, Philippines — Inilipat na sa New Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory sa Payatas si dating House Speaker Martin Romualdez. Ito ay matapos masuri ng mga doktor mula sa Philippine General Hospital na hindi na kailangan ni Romualdez ng medical needs o hospital confinement. Inilipat si Romualdez mula PGH patungo sa QC jail bandang alas-10:09 ng gabi nitong Lunes. Nahaharap si Romualdez sa P7.4 bilyong plunder dahil sa anomalya sa flood control projects. Ayon kay PGH Director Dr. Gerardo Le­gaspi, “clinically stable” si Romualdez at malabong makaranas ng emergency medical condition. Sinabi naman ni Dr. Henry Fabro, chief medical officer ng Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory, na sapat ang kanilang pasilidad sa ano mang medical needs ni Romualdez. Ayon kay Fabro, maaaring regular na gamitin ni Romualdez ang CPAP machine, gamot at maaring konsultahin ng kanyang pribadong doktor sa loob ng kulu­ngan. Maaari ring ilipat si Romualdez sa mga kalapit na ospital sakaling mayroong emergency. Itinakda naman ng Sandiganbayan Third Division ang arraignment at pre-trial ni Romualdez sa Setyembre 16, Miyerkules ng 8:30 ng umaga. Matapos na madala sa QC jail, inilabas na naman sa publiko ng Department of Interior and Local Governement ang mugshots ni Romualdez. Romualdez inside the Cardinal Santos Hospital in San Juan city last week was, of course, the result of his own cousin's SONA exposing, among others, the alleged flood-control anomalies and many allied charges. That was a landmark event in the country’s history of the administration of justice. Prosecutors state he imposed a ?2 billion monthly quota on collections. articles.title: Romualdez inilipat na sa Quezon City jail, mugshot inilabas
articles.description: Inilipat na sa New Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory sa Payatas si dating House Speaker Martin Romualdez.
articles.text: MANILA, Philippines — Inilipat na sa New Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory sa Payatas si dating House Speaker Martin Romualdez. Ito ay matapos masuri ng mga doktor mula sa Philippine General Hospital na hindi na kailangan ni Romualdez ng medical needs o hospital confinement. Inilipat si Romualdez mula PGH patungo sa QC jail bandang alas-10:09 ng gabi nitong Lunes. Nahaharap si Romualdez sa P7.4 bilyong plunder dahil sa anomalya sa flood control projects. Ayon kay PGH Director Dr. Gerardo Le­gaspi, “clinically stable” si Romualdez at malabong makaranas ng emergency medical condition. Sinabi naman ni Dr. Henry Fabro, chief medical officer ng Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory, na sapat ang kanilang pasilidad sa ano mang medical needs ni Romualdez. Ayon kay Fabro, maaaring regular na gamitin ni Romualdez ang CPAP machine, gamot at maaring konsultahin ng kanyang pribadong doktor sa loob ng kulu­ngan. Maaari ring ilipat si Romualdez sa mga kalapit na ospital sakaling mayroong emergency. Itinakda naman ng Sandiganbayan Third Division ang arraignment at pre-trial ni Romualdez sa Setyembre 16, Miyerkules ng 8:30 ng umaga. Matapos na madala sa QC jail, inilabas na naman sa publiko ng Department of Interior and Local Governement ang mugshots ni Romualdez. text.preview: Police have secured former Speaker Martin Romualdez at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan, where he was taken on Monday afternoon after suffering "a cardiovascular event, unstable blood pressure, and an anxiety attack," Interior Secretary Juanito Victor "Jovic" Remulla told reporters. Remulla went to the hospital early Monday night with PNP chief Police General Jose Melecio Nartatez to serve on Romualdez the warrant of arrest the Sandiganbayan issued after the Ombudsman filed plunder charges against the Leyte congressman, former Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co and two others. He said Romualdez is considered a person deprived of liberty once he is read his rights. "According to the doctors, he is suffering from a cardiovascular event. Unstable ang kanyang blood pressure and [he is] having an anxiety attack," Remulla said. “However, we made it clear that, like in Secretary Bonoan’s case, we will check every day hanggang he’s well enough to be presented to court," he added. “In the meantime, meron kaming armed guards outside his door. articles.title: Romualdez inilipat na sa Quezon City jail, mugshot inilabas
articles.description: Inilipat na sa New Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory sa Payatas si dating House Speaker Martin Romualdez.
articles.text: MANILA, Philippines — Inilipat na sa New Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory sa Payatas si dating House Speaker Martin Romualdez. Ito ay matapos masuri ng mga doktor mula sa Philippine General Hospital na hindi na kailangan ni Romualdez ng medical needs o hospital confinement. Inilipat si Romualdez mula PGH patungo sa QC jail bandang alas-10:09 ng gabi nitong Lunes. Nahaharap si Romualdez sa P7.4 bilyong plunder dahil sa anomalya sa flood control projects. Ayon kay PGH Director Dr. Gerardo Le­gaspi, “clinically stable” si Romualdez at malabong makaranas ng emergency medical condition. Sinabi naman ni Dr. Henry Fabro, chief medical officer ng Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory, na sapat ang kanilang pasilidad sa ano mang medical needs ni Romualdez. Ayon kay Fabro, maaaring regular na gamitin ni Romualdez ang CPAP machine, gamot at maaring konsultahin ng kanyang pribadong doktor sa loob ng kulu­ngan. Maaari ring ilipat si Romualdez sa mga kalapit na ospital sakaling mayroong emergency. Itinakda naman ng Sandiganbayan Third Division ang arraignment at pre-trial ni Romualdez sa Setyembre 16, Miyerkules ng 8:30 ng umaga. Matapos na madala sa QC jail, inilabas na naman sa publiko ng Department of Interior and Local Governement ang mugshots ni Romualdez. passages.text: Antonio Julian Montalván II is a Europe-based Filipino social anthropologist and heritage activist.
By Antonio J. Montalvan II What is it with Philippine politics that makes it so unapologetically and scandalously about self-interest in how to preserve one’s exclusive foothold on power?
For many, that is a rhetorical question;
the Filipino electorate knows the answer.
But those who think they are God’s gifts to the Filipino people can never care less for rhetorical questions.
Loren Legarda’s website is a superlative spotlight on what a gift she is to the nation—the planet rather.
Loren Legarda’s life mantra has been for the Filipino people, the country, and the planet.
She is a true Filipina at heart, passionately advocating for the protection of the rights of indigenous peoples and promoting arts and culture in the local and international arena.
She started out in the public mind as a reporter of Radio Philippines Network (RPN) during the Marcos dictatorship.

A later plum post came at ABS CBN where she was hired as co-anchor of The World Tonight newscast with Angelo Castro Jr. The network would later upgrade her as host of her own current events series The Inside Story.

Her journalism career brought her accolades: the Gawad Cultural Center of the Philippines, the Catholic Mass Media Awards Hall of Fame, the Golden Dove Award of the Kapisanan ng mga Brodkasters sa Pilipinas, the Benigno Aquino Award for Journalism, and more than 30 other awards.
The verdict was: her name recall was indubitable.
That jumpstarted the political career of this “true Filipina at heart” in 1998 when she ran for senator under the Lakas-NUCD-UMDP party.
Her presidential candidate was Jose de Venecia.
She was the topnotcher of that senatorial race with 15 million votes.
Nothing wrong with that.
Twenty-seven years later, the altruism that all neophytes swear to in serving the country needs evaluation.
The Loren Legarda we see today has mutated into a traditional politician who has alternated between the Senate and the House of Representatives to transcend term limits.
And more.
In the last elections, after she had served for one term as representative for the lone congressional seat of Antique, she fielded her younger brother Antonio Agapito “AA” Legarda to take over.
Legarda herself claims she also keeps residence in Pandan, Antique, home of her maternal grandmother’s Gella family.
For his first congressional run, AA Legarda registered his political alias as “Inday Loren.”
How long has she been known truly as Inday Loren in Antique before she had run there in 2019 after her senate term had ended?
Does she even speak Kinaray-a?
In the certified list of candidates for Antique, the brother’s name appeared as “Legarda, AA Inday Loren.”
Promptly, a resident of Bugasong town, Salvador Ungsod, petitioned the Comelec that this was a deception to Antique voters that it was Loren running.
The prayer was to declare him a nuisance candidate.
But as it is always in Philippine politics, having two family members in elective positions is not enough.
Our democracy rests on the power, not of the people, but of presiding families over cities, provinces, and districts.
And Loren Legarda has joined the drift of the fickle.
What was the price of that budding dynastic ambition?
In the present 2025 congressional race, AA Legarda is running for reelection.
Loren had to sever ties with her political allies in Antique led by the Gov. Rhodora Cadiao who was eyeing the lone congressional seat because she had completed her three terms as governor.
They had run on the same ticket in 2022.
Loren had become a determined dynast.
And why not?
Imagine the combined pork barrel benefits of a senator and a congressman.
Antique’s voters will have their hands full of campaign largesse.
The 2022 presidential campaign was said to be particularly unkind to candidate Leni Robredo in Antique.
Supporters were dismayed that the 18 municipal mayors were reportedly ordered not to extend any welcome to the vice president, including at the provincial capitol.
But the Bongbong Marcos team was given permission to use the Evelio B. Javier Freedom Park.
Javier was the martial law hero who was assassinated in cold blood by the forces of Antique kingpin and Marcos henchman Arturo Pacificador.
Who gave the order for the cold welcome to Vice President Robredo?
Antiqueños say the municipal mayors fear Loren.
She was running in the Marcos-Duterte ticket.
The coattail of the Edsa People Power she had originally run on was gone.
And then for this present electoral race, a third family member will join the two Legardas.
Leandro Legarda Leviste , the senator’s son, is running for the first congressional district of Batangas.
Readers, judge for yourselves if Legarda Leviste needs a congressional seat.
At 31 years old, the young Leviste is already worth P12B.
He is CEO of the renewable energy firm Solar Philippines (that he claims he had patterned from Elon Musk;
he had once invested in Tesla).
He is also a sugar baron through the sugar firm Roxas and Company, Inc.
(Central Azucarera de San Pedro in Nasugbu, Batangas) that he had saved from bankruptcy after buying 188.89 million shares.
Last year, Leviste’s LL Holdings Inc.
and Countryside Investment Holdings bought 10% of ABS CBN Corporation , making him the second largest shareholder of the media conglomerate after the Lopez family.
It boggles the mind why a billionaire would lust for more power beyond what he already has.
Protecting his business interests is a common script among Filipino politicians.
See where the traditional politics of Leandro’s mother had landed on the lap of this wealthy young man?
In July 2020, when the House of Representatives killed press freedom by denying the franchise of ABS CBN at the behest of Rodrigo Duterte , Representative Loren Legarda abstained.
She cited a House rule that barred bill authors from voting otherwise (her bill, House Bill 6293 , would have renewed ABS CBN’s franchise).
She claimed that the rule on conflict of interest barred her from voting to deny the franchise.
But House sources say the rule only applies to members of the legislative franchises committee who are not ex-officio members.
Legarda was ex-officio;
she was Deputy Speaker, a House big shot.
The mental gymnastics did not work.
The public instead saw an alibi that her absence during the House hearing was because of fear of Rodrigo Duterte, who had once proclaimed Leandro Leviste as a future president of the Philippines .
Loren Legarda would savor that future reality predicted by Duterte.

Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News/File MANILA ( 3RD UPDATE ) - Former House Speaker Martin Romualdez was moved to the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas on Monday night, September 14.

A transport convoy by the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) departed from the Pedro Gil exit of the University of the Philippines-Philippine General Hospital in Manila shortly after 10:00 p.m.
This comes hours after the Sandiganbayan ordered his transfer , with UP-PGH doctors finding Romualdez "clinically stable" and noting that he does not require continued hospitalization.
Upon his arrival, intake protocols began immediately.
The standard admission process that encompasses a medical evaluation, fingerprint acquisition, mugshot, interviews, and orientation is currently underway.
They said Romualdez was committed to the Quezon City Jail–Male Dormitory at approximately 10:49 p.m.
in compliance with the order of the Sandiganbayan 3rd Division.

"Considering his medical needs and the medical recommendations presented before the Court, Rep. Romualdez has been placed in the jail infirmary together with other PDL requiring medical monitoring," the BJMP said in a statement.
"The arrangement is in accordance with BJMP policies and the Court’s directives to ensure that his continuing medical needs are properly attended to," it added.

"The BJMP assures the public that it will remain professional, impartial, and consistent in the implementation of its rules and regulations. All PDL under its custody are treated fairly and humanely, without distinction or privilege based on status or position."
PLUNDER CASE Romualdez was arrested last Monday, September 7, after the Sandiganbayan issued a warrant for the P7.4-billion plunder case filed by the Ombudsman.
He was initially confined at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center before being transferred to UP-PGH on Saturday for an independent examination.

READ: PGH finishing medical exams on Martin Romualdez Dr. Gerardo Legaspi, medical director of UP-PGH, took the witness stand on Monday during the Sandiganbayan Third Division's hearing on Romualdez's motion for continued confinement.
When Associate Justice Ronald Moreno asked if Romualdez could be discharged from the hospital at any time, Legaspi answered in the affirmative.
Romualdez is expected to stay in a cell that is about 50 square meters, with five double-deck beds.
The BJMP said it was also considering Romualdez's medical condition and security concerns in determining his placement.
Under BJMP policy, PDLs with certain medical or psychiatric conditions and comorbidities should not be left alone in a cell.
Romualdez said in a statement on Monday that he respects the court's decision, but maintains his innocence .

Revoli Cortez, PPA pool/File MANILA—Malacañang maintained Tuesday that there should be no special treatment and that the law must be equally applied to all accused in the wake of former House Speaker Martin Romualdez's transfer to the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas.
Romualdez was moved to the QC jail on Monday night, hours after the Sandiganbayan ordered his transfer.
Doctors of the University of the Philippines-Philippine General Hospital had found the former house speaker "clinically stable."
READ: Martin Romualdez transferred to QC jail in Payatas Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said she has yet to talk with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. over his cousin's imprisonment.

"Kahit po nasa kulungan sinuman, in general po, ito ating isasagot: Hangga't wala pa po kasing naibibigay na paghuhusga with finality ang isang korte, ang presumption pa rin po niyan ay inosente sila. Nagkataon lang po na ang mga kasong kinakaharap nila ay no bail, no bail recommended ang ibinibigay at sinasabi at pinag-uutos ng korte," she said in a press briefing Tuesday, September 15.

"Kung ano po ang sinasapit ngayon ng mga diumanong sangkot, iyan naman po ay walang dapat sinisino – mayaman, mahirap, ordinaryong tao, may kapangyarihan. Kung nakagawa man ng mali sa taumbayan, kailangan lang din pong pantay-pantay kung ano po ang naranasan ng mga akusado," Castro added.
"So wala pong dapat na special treatment. Hindi po kinakailangang mag-rally kung saan-saan para hindi mapanagot ang sinuman, dapat po pantay-pantay."
Castro maintained that the Marcos administration is all for following the law and proper process of all accused regardless of their status.

passages.text: peaker Martin Romualdez delivers his speech as he steps down from his post as Speaker of the House of Representatives on Wednesday, September 17, 2025.
Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News/File MANILA ( 3RD UPDATE ) - Former House Speaker Martin Romualdez was moved to the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas on Monday night, September 14.

A transport convoy by the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) departed from the Pedro Gil exit of the University of the Philippines-Philippine General Hospital in Manila shortly after 10:00 p.m.
This comes hours after the Sandiganbayan ordered his transfer , with UP-PGH doctors finding Romualdez "clinically stable" and noting that he does not require continued hospitalization.
Upon his arrival, intake protocols began immediately.
The standard admission process that encompasses a medical evaluation, fingerprint acquisition, mugshot, interviews, and orientation is currently underway.
They said Romualdez was committed to the Quezon City Jail–Male Dormitory at approximately 10:49 p.m.
in compliance with the order of the Sandiganbayan 3rd Division.

"Considering his medical needs and the medical recommendations presented before the Court, Rep. Romualdez has been placed in the jail infirmary together with other PDL requiring medical monitoring," the BJMP said in a statement.
"The arrangement is in accordance with BJMP policies and the Court’s directives to ensure that his continuing medical needs are properly attended to," it added.

"The BJMP assures the public that it will remain professional, impartial, and consistent in the implementation of its rules and regulations. All PDL under its custody are treated fairly and humanely, without distinction or privilege based on status or position."
PLUNDER CASE Romualdez was arrested last Monday, September 7, after the Sandiganbayan issued a warrant for the P7.4-billion plunder case filed by the Ombudsman.
He was initially confined at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center before being transferred to UP-PGH on Saturday for an independent examination.

READ: PGH finishing medical exams on Martin Romualdez Dr. Gerardo Legaspi, medical director of UP-PGH, took the witness stand on Monday during the Sandiganbayan Third Division's hearing on Romualdez's motion for continued confinement.
When Associate Justice Ronald Moreno asked if Romualdez could be discharged from the hospital at any time, Legaspi answered in the affirmative.
Romualdez is expected to stay in a cell that is about 50 square meters, with five double-deck beds.
The BJMP said it was also considering Romualdez's medical condition and security concerns in determining his placement.
Under BJMP policy, PDLs with certain medical or psychiatric conditions and comorbidities should not be left alone in a cell.
Romualdez said in a statement on Monday that he respects the court's decision, but maintains his innocence .
RELATED VIDEO:
Presidential Communications Office Usec.
Claire Castro during a press briefing in Malacañang Palace in Manila on July 18, 2025.

Revoli Cortez, PPA pool/File MANILA—Malacañang maintained Tuesday that there should be no special treatment and that the law must be equally applied to all accused in the wake of former House Speaker Martin Romualdez's transfer to the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas.
Romualdez was moved to the QC jail on Monday night, hours after the Sandiganbayan ordered his transfer.
Doctors of the University of the Philippines-Philippine General Hospital had found the former house speaker "clinically stable."
READ: Martin Romualdez transferred to QC jail in Payatas Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said she has yet to talk with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. over his cousin's imprisonment.

"Kahit po nasa kulungan sinuman, in general po, ito ating isasagot: Hangga't wala pa po kasing naibibigay na paghuhusga with finality ang isang korte, ang presumption pa rin po niyan ay inosente sila. Nagkataon lang po na ang mga kasong kinakaharap nila ay no bail, no bail recommended ang ibinibigay at sinasabi at pinag-uutos ng korte," she said in a press briefing Tuesday, September 15.

"Kung ano po ang sinasapit ngayon ng mga diumanong sangkot, iyan naman po ay walang dapat sinisino – mayaman, mahirap, ordinaryong tao, may kapangyarihan. Kung nakagawa man ng mali sa taumbayan, kailangan lang din pong pantay-pantay kung ano po ang naranasan ng mga akusado," Castro added.
"So wala pong dapat na special treatment. Hindi po kinakailangang mag-rally kung saan-saan para hindi mapanagot ang sinuman, dapat po pantay-pantay."
Castro maintained that the Marcos administration is all for following the law and proper process of all accused regardless of their status.
"Hindi kailangang umabuso, hindi naman kailangang kulang ang pagtrato sa maaaring nasasangkot. So, dapat lang po ay kung ano iyong naaayon sa batas at proseso," she said.
Asked if Malacañang would encourage the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology to release more photos of Romualdez for transparency, Castro said it is up to the Bureau's discretion.
"Nasa pamumuno na po nila iyan. Kung ano po ang nakikita nilang nararapat, as long na ang mga akusado ay nasa kustodiya po nila, nasa kanilang kamay na po ang pagpapasiya niyan," she stated.
CANCELLED PGH VISIT Marcos was scheduled to have a visit to the Philippine General Hospital on Monday, September 14 but was cancelled Sunday night.
Pressed why, Castro cited conflict in schedule with Marcos Jr. coming home from his participation in the recently concluded 18th BRICS Summit in India early Monday morning.

"Kagagaling lang po kasi kagabi, madaling araw po dumating ang Pangulo. Alam ninyo naman po na halos mag-aalas singko na po dumating ang Pangulo. Hindi po naipagbigay—nabigay pabatid or nabigyan tayo ng kaalaman tungkol sa anong oras supposed to be kung pupunta man siya sa PGH, kasi kagagaling lang po niya sa India, kakatapos lang po ng kanyang trabaho at halos mag-aalas singko na po ng madaling araw dumating ang Pangulo," she said.
The Palace official also denied that it had something to do with Romualdez who was then confined in the facility for an independent medical examination as ordered by the Sandiganbayan Third Division.

"Wala. Walang napag-usapan patungkol diyan na iyon ang magiging dahilan. Nagkataon lang po siguro na kararating lang ng Pangulo, ng halos mag-aalas singko na po ng madaling araw, wala pa pong tulog iyon halos," she said.
RELATED VIDEO:
MANILA, Philippines — Inilipat na sa New Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory sa Payatas si dating House Speaker Martin Romualdez.
Ito ay matapos masuri ng mga doktor mula sa Philippine General Hospital na hindi na kailangan ni Romualdez ng medical needs o hospital confinement.
Inilipat si Romualdez mula PGH patungo sa QC jail bandang alas-10:09 ng gabi nitong Lunes.
Nahaharap si Romualdez sa P7.4 bilyong plunder dahil sa anomalya sa flood control projects.
Ayon kay PGH Director Dr. Gerardo Le­gaspi, “clinically stable” si Romualdez at malabong makaranas ng emergency medical condition.
Sinabi naman ni Dr. Henry Fabro, chief medical officer ng Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory, na sapat ang kanilang pasilidad sa ano mang medical needs ni Romualdez.
Ayon kay Fabro, maaaring regular na gamitin ni Romualdez ang CPAP machine, gamot at maaring konsultahin ng kanyang pribadong doktor sa loob ng kulu­ngan.
Maaari ring ilipat si Romualdez sa mga kalapit na ospital sakaling mayroong emergency.
Itinakda naman ng Sandiganbayan Third Division ang arraignment at pre-trial ni Romualdez sa Setyembre 16, Miyerkules ng 8:30 ng umaga.
Matapos na madala sa QC jail, inilabas na naman sa publiko ng Department of Interior and Local Governement ang mugshots ni Romualdez.

text.preview: Antonio Julian Montalván II is a Europe-based Filipino social anthropologist and heritage activist. By Antonio J. Montalvan II What is it with Philippine politics that makes it so unapologetically and scandalously about self-interest in how to preserve one’s exclusive foothold on power? For many, that is a rhetorical question; the Filipino electorate knows the answer. But those who think they are God’s gifts to the Filipino people can never care less for rhetorical questions. Loren Legarda’s website is a superlative spotlight on what a gift she is to the nation—the planet rather. Loren Legarda’s life mantra has been for the Filipino people, the country, and the planet. She is a true Filipina at heart, passionately advocating for the protection of the rights of indigenous peoples and promoting arts and culture in the local and international arena. She started out in the public mind as a reporter of Radio Philippines Network (RPN) during the Marcos dictatorship. A later plum post came at ABS CBN where she was hired as co-anchor of The World Tonight newscast with Angelo Castro Jr. The network would later upgrade her as host of her own current events series The Inside Story. Her journalism career brought her accolades: the Gawad Cultural Center of the Philippines, the Catholic Mass Media Awards Hall of Fame, the Golden Dove Award of the Kapisanan ng mga Brodkasters sa Pilipinas, the Benigno Aquino Award for Journalism, and more than 30 other awards. The verdict was: her name recall was indubitable. That jumpstarted the political career of this “true Filipina at heart” in 1998 when she ran for senator under the Lakas-NUCD-UMDP party. Her presidential candidate was Jose de Venecia. She was the topnotcher of that senatorial race with 15 million votes. Nothing wrong with that. Twenty-seven years later, the altruism that all neophytes swear to in serving the country needs evaluation. According to the BJMP, Romualdez arrived at the Payatas facility at 10:49 p.m. He will undergo standard booking procedures: medical evaluation, fingerprinting, mugshot, interview, and orientation. In a statement, the BJMP said Romualdez was placed in the jail infirmary . "Considering his medical needs and the medical recommendations presented before the Court, Rep. Romualdez has been placed in the jail infirmary together with other [persons deprived of liberty] requiring medical monitoring," the BJMP said. The BJMP said the arrangement is in accordance with BJMP policies and the Sandiganbayan’s directives to ensure that his continuing medical needs are properly attended to. Romualdez faces plunder charges over P7.2 billion in alleged kickbacks from government infrastructure projects. His co-accused, former Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co, Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp. president Felicito Guevarra, and Romualdez’s personal assistant Joselin Sereño are all at large. Other officials facing plunder before the Sandiganbayan who are detained at the QC Jail in Payatas include Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta. Also in the said jail is former Anak Kalusugan party-list Rep. Michael Defensor. In a statement, Romualdez said he respects the Sandiganbayan’s decision. “I have always said that I will face the charges against me and answer them before the proper court. Police have secured former Speaker Martin Romualdez at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan, where he was taken on Monday afternoon after suffering "a cardiovascular event, unstable blood pressure, and an anxiety attack," Interior Secretary Juanito Victor "Jovic" Remulla told reporters. Remulla went to the hospital early Monday night with PNP chief Police General Jose Melecio Nartatez to serve on Romualdez the warrant of arrest the Sandiganbayan issued after the Ombudsman filed plunder charges against the Leyte congressman, former Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co and two others. He said Romualdez is considered a person deprived of liberty once he is read his rights. "According to the doctors, he is suffering from a cardiovascular event. Unstable ang kanyang blood pressure and [he is] having an anxiety attack," Remulla said. “However, we made it clear that, like in Secretary Bonoan’s case, we will check every day hanggang he’s well enough to be presented to court," he added. “In the meantime, meron kaming armed guards outside his door. Meron kaming armed police outside the hospital and in the lobby," Remulla said. “After we read him his rights, he is now considered a person deprived of liberty," he added. The arrest of former speaker Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez inside the Cardinal Santos Hospital in San Juan city last week was, of course, the result of his own cousin's SONA exposing, among others, the alleged flood-control anomalies and many allied charges. That was a landmark event in the country’s history of the administration of justice. Never before in Philippine history has a former speaker of the House been charged and arrested upon the clearance of the president who happens to be his first-degree cousin. It has not been an easy move on the part of president BBM who is not known to be a violent or vengeful man but a compassionate and kind-hearted person. Not many expected that Romualdez would be charged with plunder, which is a non-bailable offense, aside from direct and indirect bribery and money laundering. That means that after his medical issues are properly addressed, he will be brought to the Quezon City detention center in Payatas to join the others, Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta, The arrest of Romualdez and his co-accused was based on the allegations that the former speaker allegedly received kickbacks and commissions on at least 15 occasions between 2022 and 2025. Prosecutors state he imposed a ?2 billion monthly quota on collections. The money was allegedly laundered through shell companies like Golden Pheasant Holdings, Bravos Holdings, and Valiant Consolidated Resource Ferdinand Martin Romualdez, born on November 14, 1963, is the third child of Madam Imelda Marcos' favorite brother Benjamin Kokoy Romualdez, former governor of Leyte and ambassador to the U.S. He is a graduate of UP Law, and Cornell and Harvard universities. For many, that is a rhetorical question; the Filipino electorate knows the answer. But those who think they are God’s gifts to the Filipino people can never care less for rhetorical questions. Loren Legarda’s website is a superlative spotlight on what a gift she is to the nation—the planet rather. Loren Legarda’s life mantra has been for the Filipino people, the country, and the planet. She is a true Filipina at heart, passionately advocating for the protection of the rights of indigenous peoples and promoting arts and culture in the local and international arena. She started out in the public mind as a reporter of Radio Philippines Network (RPN) during the Marcos dictatorship. Her journalism career brought her accolades: the Gawad Cultural Center of the Philippines, the Catholic Mass Media Awards Hall of Fame, the Golden Dove Award of the Kapisanan ng mga Brodkasters sa Pilipinas, the Benigno Aquino Award for Journalism, and more than 30 other awards. The verdict was: her name recall was indubitable. That jumpstarted the political career of this “true Filipina at heart” in 1998 when she ran for senator under the Lakas-NUCD-UMDP party. Her presidential candidate was Jose de Venecia. She was the topnotcher of that senatorial race with 15 million votes. Nothing wrong with that. article.title: Romualdez inilipat na sa Quezon City jail, mugshot inilabas
article.description: Inilipat na sa New Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory sa Payatas si dating House Speaker Martin Romualdez.
article.text: MANILA, Philippines — Inilipat na sa New Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory sa Payatas si dating House Speaker Martin Romualdez. Ito ay matapos masuri ng mga doktor mula sa Philippine General Hospital na hindi na kailangan ni Romualdez ng medical needs o hospital confinement. Inilipat si Romualdez mula PGH patungo sa QC jail bandang alas-10:09 ng gabi nitong Lunes. Nahaharap si Romualdez sa P7.4 bilyong plunder dahil sa anomalya sa flood control projects. Ayon kay PGH Director Dr. Gerardo Le­gaspi, “clinically stable” si Romualdez at malabong makaranas ng emergency medical condition. Sinabi naman ni Dr. Henry Fabro, chief medical officer ng Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory, na sapat ang kanilang pasilidad sa ano mang medical needs ni Romualdez. Ayon kay Fabro, maaaring regular na gamitin ni Romualdez ang CPAP machine, gamot at maaring konsultahin ng kanyang pribadong doktor sa loob ng kulu­ngan. Maaari ring ilipat si Romualdez sa mga kalapit na ospital sakaling mayroong emergency. Itinakda naman ng Sandiganbayan Third Division ang arraignment at pre-trial ni Romualdez sa Setyembre 16, Miyerkules ng 8:30 ng umaga. Matapos na madala sa QC jail, inilabas na naman sa publiko ng Department of Interior and Local Governement ang mugshots ni Romualdez. output.title: Martin Romualdez transferred to QC jail in Payatas | ABS-CBN News
output.description: Former House Speaker Martin Romualdez is now at the Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory in Payatas, after leaving the University of the Philippines-Philippine Gener
output.text: peaker Martin Romualdez delivers his speech as he steps down from his post as Speaker of the House of Representatives on Wednesday, September 17, 2025. Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News/File MANILA ( 3RD UPDATE ) - Former House Speaker Martin Romualdez was moved to the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas on Monday night, September 14. A transport convoy by the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) departed from the Pedro Gil exit of the University of the Philippines-Philippine General Hospital in Manila shortly after 10:00 p.m. This comes hours after the Sandiganbayan ordered his transfer , with UP-PGH doctors finding Romualdez "clinically stable" and noting that he does not require continued hospitalization. Upon his arrival, intake protocols began immediately. The standard admission process that encompasses a medical evaluation, fingerprint acquisition, mugshot, interviews, and orientation is currently underway. They said Romualdez was committed to the Quezon City Jail–Male Dormitory at approximately 10:49 p.m. in compliance with the order of the Sandiganbayan 3rd Division. "Considering his medical needs and the medical recommendations presented before the Court, Rep. Romualdez has been placed in the jail infirmary together with other PDL requiring medical monitoring," the BJMP said in a statement. "The arrangement is in accordance with BJMP policies and the Court’s directives to ensure that his continuing medical needs are properly attended to," it added. "The BJMP assures the public that it will remain professional, impartial, and consistent in the implementation of its rules and regulations. All PDL under its custody are treated fairly and humanely, without distinction or privilege based on status or position." PLUNDER CASE Romualdez was arrested last Monday, September 7, after the Sandiganbayan issued a warrant for the P7.4-billion plunder case filed by the Ombudsman. He was initially confined at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center before being transferred to UP-PGH on Saturday for an independent examination. READ: PGH finishing medical exams on Martin Romualdez Dr. Gerardo Legaspi, medical director of UP-PGH, took the witness stand on Monday during the Sandiganbayan Third Division's hearing on Romualdez's motion for continued confinement. When Associate Justice Ronald Moreno asked if Romualdez could be discharged from the hospital at any time, Legaspi answered in the affirmative. Romualdez is expected to stay in a cell that is about 50 square meters, with five double-deck beds. The BJMP said it was also considering Romualdez's medical condition and security concerns in determining his placement. Under BJMP policy, PDLs with certain medical or psychiatric conditions and comorbidities should not be left alone in a cell. Romualdez said in a statement on Monday that he respects the court's decision, but maintains his innocence . RELATED VIDEO:

output.text: Former Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez has arrived at the Quezon City Jail, the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology has said. According to the BJMP, Romualdez arrived at the Payatas facility at 10:49 p.m. He will undergo standard booking procedures: medical evaluation, fingerprinting, mugshot, interview, and orientation. In a statement, the BJMP said Romualdez was placed in the jail infirmary . "Considering his medical needs and the medical recommendations presented before the Court, Rep. Romualdez has been placed in the jail infirmary together with other [persons deprived of liberty] requiring medical monitoring," the BJMP said. The BJMP said the arrangement is in accordance with BJMP policies and the Sandiganbayan’s directives to ensure that his continuing medical needs are properly attended to. Romualdez faces plunder charges over P7.2 billion in alleged kickbacks from government infrastructure projects. His co-accused, former Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co, Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp. president Felicito Guevarra, and Romualdez’s personal assistant Joselin Sereño are all at large. Other officials facing plunder before the Sandiganbayan who are detained at the QC Jail in Payatas include Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta. Also in the said jail is former Anak Kalusugan party-list Rep. Michael Defensor. In a statement, Romualdez said he respects the Sandiganbayan’s decision. “I have always said that I will face the charges against me and answer them before the proper court. That has not changed,” he said. “I maintain my innocence. Haharapin ko ang kaso. Sasagutin ko ang mga paratang,” he added. (I maintain my innocence. I will face the case. I will answer the allegations.) He also extended his gratitude to the doctors. The Sandiganbayan on Monday committed Romualdez to the male dormitory of the Quezon City Jail. He had been in the hospital since his arrest. First, in the Cardinal Santos Medical Center, and then in the Philippine General Hospital. Doctors from the PGH on Monday told the Sandiganbayan that his condition was stable enough so as not to require being confined in the hospital. In its order dated September 14, the Third Division also set his arraignment on Wednesday, September 16. "Accordingly, the court commits to the Quezon City Jail - Male Dormitory the living person of accused Romualdez, who is charged for the crime of plunder, to be held therein as a detention prisoner and as such, the accused shall not be moved, removed, transferred, and/or otherwise be released therefrom unless ordered by the court," the court said. "The parties are reminded that the arraignment and pre-trial of this case as to accused Romualdez si set on Wednesday, September 16, 2026 at 8:30 in the morning," it added. –NB GMA News

output.title: Police secure Martin Romualdez at Cardinal Santos, says DILG chief Remulla
output.description: Former Speaker Martin Romualdez was taken to the Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan on Monday with a "cardiovascular event, unstable blood pressure, and anxiety attack," Interior Secretary Juanito Victor "Jonvic Remulla said. “In the meantime, meron kaming armed guards outside his door. Meron kaming armed police outside the hospital and in the lobby," Remulla said.
output.text: Police have secured former Speaker Martin Romualdez at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan, where he was taken on Monday afternoon after suffering "a cardiovascular event, unstable blood pressure, and an anxiety attack," Interior Secretary Juanito Victor "Jovic" Remulla told reporters. Remulla went to the hospital early Monday night with PNP chief Police General Jose Melecio Nartatez to serve on Romualdez the warrant of arrest the Sandiganbayan issued after the Ombudsman filed plunder charges against the Leyte congressman, former Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co and two others. He said Romualdez is considered a person deprived of liberty once he is read his rights. "According to the doctors, he is suffering from a cardiovascular event. Unstable ang kanyang blood pressure and [he is] having an anxiety attack," Remulla said. “However, we made it clear that, like in Secretary Bonoan’s case, we will check every day hanggang he’s well enough to be presented to court," he added. “In the meantime, meron kaming armed guards outside his door. Meron kaming armed police outside the hospital and in the lobby," Remulla said. “After we read him his rights, he is now considered a person deprived of liberty," he added. P7.4B plunder charge The Office of the Ombudsman on Monday filed a P7.4-billion plunder charge against Romualdez, former House appropriations panel chairperson Zaldy Co of Ako Bicol party-list, Joselyn Tragua Serenio, who is the personal assistant of Romualdez, and Felicito Cristobal Guevarra, president of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corporation. “By repeatedly receiving, directly or indirectly, on at least 15 occasions, commissions, shares, percentages. kickbacks, "commitments." and/or other pecuniary benefits aggregating at least P7.4 billion by reason or on account of the respective public offices and positions of Romualdez and Co, including monies derived from contractors, persons and entities with interests in flood control, infrastructure and/or other government projects funded under the General Appropriations Acts for fiscal years 2022 to 2025, which monies were delivered to properties owned by, occupied by, or associated with Romualdez and received by Serenio and other persons acting for and in his behalf,” the criminal information read. The Sandiganbayan Third Division hours later on Monday issued warrants of arrest against them. "The issuance of a warrant of arrest signifies only that, after personally evaluating the records, the Court found probable cause to believe that the accused committed the offense charged," the Third Division said. "Probable cause for the issuance of a warrant of arrest exists when the facts and circumstances alleged by the prosecution would lead a reasonably discreet and prudent person to believe that an offense has been committed by the person sought to be arrested," it added. Remulla said the hospital arrest was not a "permanent situation" for the former Speaker. "But we assure you, we assure you, he cannot hide behind his wealth," Remulla said. He said Romualdez's cell at the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas is waiting if the Sandiganbayan would commit him to the detention facility. Fair shake A lawyer for Romualdez said he would face all allegations against him in connection with his alleged links to the kickback scheme involving the flood control mess. “We respect the courts and the legal process. Representative Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez will face the allegations against him in accordance with law,” Atty. Ade Fajardo, counsel of Romualdez, said in a statement. “We recognize the public interest surrounding this case. But ultimately, criminal liability must be determined by the evidence presented in court, under the rules and safeguards of our justice system,” he added. He also said that Romualdez, a cousin of President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos, Jr., only asked for a fair shake. –NB GMA News

output.title: Loren Legarda fattens her dynasty
output.description: In the certified list of candidates for Antique Representative, the name of Sen. Loren Legarda’s brother appeared as “Legarda, AA Inday Loren.”
output.text: Antonio Julian Montalván II is a Europe-based Filipino social anthropologist and heritage activist. By Antonio J. Montalvan II What is it with Philippine politics that makes it so unapologetically and scandalously about self-interest in how to preserve one’s exclusive foothold on power? For many, that is a rhetorical question; the Filipino electorate knows the answer. But those who think they are God’s gifts to the Filipino people can never care less for rhetorical questions. Loren Legarda’s website is a superlative spotlight on what a gift she is to the nation—the planet rather. Loren Legarda’s life mantra has been for the Filipino people, the country, and the planet. She is a true Filipina at heart, passionately advocating for the protection of the rights of indigenous peoples and promoting arts and culture in the local and international arena. She started out in the public mind as a reporter of Radio Philippines Network (RPN) during the Marcos dictatorship. A later plum post came at ABS CBN where she was hired as co-anchor of The World Tonight newscast with Angelo Castro Jr. The network would later upgrade her as host of her own current events series The Inside Story. Her journalism career brought her accolades: the Gawad Cultural Center of the Philippines, the Catholic Mass Media Awards Hall of Fame, the Golden Dove Award of the Kapisanan ng mga Brodkasters sa Pilipinas, the Benigno Aquino Award for Journalism, and more than 30 other awards. The verdict was: her name recall was indubitable. That jumpstarted the political career of this “true Filipina at heart” in 1998 when she ran for senator under the Lakas-NUCD-UMDP party. Her presidential candidate was Jose de Venecia. She was the topnotcher of that senatorial race with 15 million votes. Nothing wrong with that. Twenty-seven years later, the altruism that all neophytes swear to in serving the country needs evaluation. The Loren Legarda we see today has mutated into a traditional politician who has alternated between the Senate and the House of Representatives to transcend term limits. And more. In the last elections, after she had served for one term as representative for the lone congressional seat of Antique, she fielded her younger brother Antonio Agapito “AA” Legarda to take over. Legarda herself claims she also keeps residence in Pandan, Antique, home of her maternal grandmother’s Gella family. For his first congressional run, AA Legarda registered his political alias as “Inday Loren.” How long has she been known truly as Inday Loren in Antique before she had run there in 2019 after her senate term had ended? Does she even speak Kinaray-a? In the certified list of candidates for Antique, the brother’s name appeared as “Legarda, AA Inday Loren.” Promptly, a resident of Bugasong town, Salvador Ungsod, petitioned the Comelec that this was a deception to Antique voters that it was Loren running. The prayer was to declare him a nuisance candidate. But as it is always in Philippine politics, having two family members in elective positions is not enough. Our democracy rests on the power, not of the people, but of presiding families over cities, provinces, and districts. And Loren Legarda has joined the drift of the fickle. What was the price of that budding dynastic ambition? In the present 2025 congressional race, AA Legarda is running for reelection. Loren had to sever ties with her political allies in Antique led by the Gov. Rhodora Cadiao who was eyeing the lone congressional seat because she had completed her three terms as governor. They had run on the same ticket in 2022. Loren had become a determined dynast. And why not? Imagine the combined pork barrel benefits of a senator and a congressman. Antique’s voters will have their hands full of campaign largesse. The 2022 presidential campaign was said to be particularly unkind to candidate Leni Robredo in Antique. Supporters were dismayed that the 18 municipal mayors were reportedly ordered not to extend any welcome to the vice president, including at the provincial capitol. But the Bongbong Marcos team was given permission to use the Evelio B. Javier Freedom Park. Javier was the martial law hero who was assassinated in cold blood by the forces of Antique kingpin and Marcos henchman Arturo Pacificador. Who gave the order for the cold welcome to Vice President Robredo? Antiqueños say the municipal mayors fear Loren. She was running in the Marcos-Duterte ticket. The coattail of the Edsa People Power she had originally run on was gone. And then for this present electoral race, a third family member will join the two Legardas. Leandro Legarda Leviste , the senator’s son, is running for the first congressional district of Batangas. Readers, judge for yourselves if Legarda Leviste needs a congressional seat. At 31 years old, the young Leviste is already worth P12B. He is CEO of the renewable energy firm Solar Philippines (that he claims he had patterned from Elon Musk; he had once invested in Tesla). He is also a sugar baron through the sugar firm Roxas and Company, Inc. (Central Azucarera de San Pedro in Nasugbu, Batangas) that he had saved from bankruptcy after buying 188.89 million shares. Last year, Leviste’s LL Holdings Inc. and Countryside Investment Holdings bought 10% of ABS CBN Corporation , making him the second largest shareholder of the media conglomerate after the Lopez family. It boggles the mind why a billionaire would lust for more power beyond what he already has. Protecting his business interests is a common script among Filipino politicians. See where the traditional politics of Leandro’s mother had landed on the lap of this wealthy young man? In July 2020, when the House of Representatives killed press freedom by denying the franchise of ABS CBN at the behest of Rodrigo Duterte , Representative Loren Legarda abstained. She cited a House rule that barred bill authors from voting otherwise (her bill, House Bill 6293 , would have renewed ABS CBN’s franchise). She claimed that the rule on conflict of interest barred her from voting to deny the franchise. But House sources say the rule only applies to members of the legislative franchises committee who are not ex-officio members. Legarda was ex-officio; she was Deputy Speaker, a House big shot. The mental gymnastics did not work. The public instead saw an alibi that her absence during the House hearing was because of fear of Rodrigo Duterte, who had once proclaimed Leandro Leviste as a future president of the Philippines . Loren Legarda would savor that future reality predicted by Duterte. The views in this column are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the views of VERA Files . output.title: On cousins Martin Romualdez & Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.
output.description: The arrest of former speaker Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez inside the Cardinal Santos Hospital in San Juan city last week was, of course, the result of his own cousin's SONA exposing, among others, the alleged flood-control anomalies and many allied charges.
output.text: The arrest of former speaker Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez inside the Cardinal Santos Hospital in San Juan city last week was, of course, the result of his own cousin's SONA exposing, among others, the alleged flood-control anomalies and many allied charges. That was a landmark event in the country’s history of the administration of justice. Never before in Philippine history has a former speaker of the House been charged and arrested upon the clearance of the president who happens to be his first-degree cousin. It has not been an easy move on the part of president BBM who is not known to be a violent or vengeful man but a compassionate and kind-hearted person. Not many expected that Romualdez would be charged with plunder, which is a non-bailable offense, aside from direct and indirect bribery and money laundering. That means that after his medical issues are properly addressed, he will be brought to the Quezon City detention center in Payatas to join the others, Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta, The arrest of Romualdez and his co-accused was based on the allegations that the former speaker allegedly received kickbacks and commissions on at least 15 occasions between 2022 and 2025. Prosecutors state he imposed a ?2 billion monthly quota on collections. The money was allegedly laundered through shell companies like Golden Pheasant Holdings, Bravos Holdings, and Valiant Consolidated Resource Ferdinand Martin Romualdez, born on November 14, 1963, is the third child of Madam Imelda Marcos' favorite brother Benjamin Kokoy Romualdez, former governor of Leyte and ambassador to the U.S. He is a graduate of UP Law, and Cornell and Harvard universities. He became a lawyer in 1993. He is married to Yedda Marie Mendoza Kittilstvedt who is also an incumbent member of Congress along with his son. Another son is a councilor of Tacloban. He was speaker from 2022 to 2025. Ferdinand Romualdez Marcos Jr, or BBM, born on September 13, 1957, is the only son of the late Ferdinand Edralin Marcos Sr. and Madam Imelda. Since he has no brother, BBM is close to his male cousins including Ferdinand Martin. Incidentally, the former speaker's father, Kokoy, named him Ferdinand Martin in honor of Ferdinand Marcos who helped Kokoy become Leyte governor and U.S. ambassador. It pains BBM too much to have to allow the charges to be filed against his own esteemed first cousin, and it pains Martin even much more to be "betrayed" by his close relative. But it appears that the evidence calls for the charges to be filed. No one is above the law. There should be no selective justice. Let justice be done though the heavens may fall, so to say. If Kokoy were alive today, and if Madam Imelda were in her prime at these times, the two would have raised hell to prevent all this by all means. I have my own thesis also, that all this was also planned and cleared by the first lady who is a brilliant lawyer herself and a Law professor at that. The first lady is just trying to protect the administration of President BBM. Charging Martin is biting the bullet and crossing the Rubicon. There shall be no turning back. The link between the Marcoses and the Romualdez clan will never be the same again. What matters most is that such a draconian move is definitely good for the Filipino people. output.title: Romualdez inilipat na sa Quezon City jail, mugshot inilabas
output.description: Inilipat na sa New Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory sa Payatas si dating House Speaker Martin Romualdez.
output.text: MANILA, Philippines — Inilipat na sa New Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory sa Payatas si dating House Speaker Martin Romualdez. Ito ay matapos masuri ng mga doktor mula sa Philippine General Hospital na hindi na kailangan ni Romualdez ng medical needs o hospital confinement. Inilipat si Romualdez mula PGH patungo sa QC jail bandang alas-10:09 ng gabi nitong Lunes. Nahaharap si Romualdez sa P7.4 bilyong plunder dahil sa anomalya sa flood control projects. Ayon kay PGH Director Dr. Gerardo Le­gaspi, “clinically stable” si Romualdez at malabong makaranas ng emergency medical condition. Sinabi naman ni Dr. Henry Fabro, chief medical officer ng Quezon City Jail Male Dormitory, na sapat ang kanilang pasilidad sa ano mang medical needs ni Romualdez. Ayon kay Fabro, maaaring regular na gamitin ni Romualdez ang CPAP machine, gamot at maaring konsultahin ng kanyang pribadong doktor sa loob ng kulu­ngan. Maaari ring ilipat si Romualdez sa mga kalapit na ospital sakaling mayroong emergency. Itinakda naman ng Sandiganbayan Third Division ang arraignment at pre-trial ni Romualdez sa Setyembre 16, Miyerkules ng 8:30 ng umaga. Matapos na madala sa QC jail, inilabas na naman sa publiko ng Department of Interior and Local Governement ang mugshots ni Romualdez. output.title: Law must be applied equally to all accused, says Malacañang after Romualdez's transfer to QC jail | ABS-CBN News
output.description: Malacañang maintained Tuesday that there should be no special treatment and that the law must be equally applied to all accused in the wake of former House Spea
output.text: Presidential Communications Office Usec. Claire Castro during a press briefing in Malacañang Palace in Manila on July 18, 2025. Revoli Cortez, PPA pool/File MANILA—Malacañang maintained Tuesday that there should be no special treatment and that the law must be equally applied to all accused in the wake of former House Speaker Martin Romualdez's transfer to the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas. Romualdez was moved to the QC jail on Monday night, hours after the Sandiganbayan ordered his transfer. Doctors of the University of the Philippines-Philippine General Hospital had found the former house speaker "clinically stable." READ: Martin Romualdez transferred to QC jail in Payatas Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said she has yet to talk with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. over his cousin's imprisonment. "Kahit po nasa kulungan sinuman, in general po, ito ating isasagot: Hangga't wala pa po kasing naibibigay na paghuhusga with finality ang isang korte, ang presumption pa rin po niyan ay inosente sila. Nagkataon lang po na ang mga kasong kinakaharap nila ay no bail, no bail recommended ang ibinibigay at sinasabi at pinag-uutos ng korte," she said in a press briefing Tuesday, September 15. "Kung ano po ang sinasapit ngayon ng mga diumanong sangkot, iyan naman po ay walang dapat sinisino – mayaman, mahirap, ordinaryong tao, may kapangyarihan. Kung nakagawa man ng mali sa taumbayan, kailangan lang din pong pantay-pantay kung ano po ang naranasan ng mga akusado," Castro added. "So wala pong dapat na special treatment. Hindi po kinakailangang mag-rally kung saan-saan para hindi mapanagot ang sinuman, dapat po pantay-pantay." Castro maintained that the Marcos administration is all for following the law and proper process of all accused regardless of their status. "Hindi kailangang umabuso, hindi naman kailangang kulang ang pagtrato sa maaaring nasasangkot. So, dapat lang po ay kung ano iyong naaayon sa batas at proseso," she said. Asked if Malacañang would encourage the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology to release more photos of Romualdez for transparency, Castro said it is up to the Bureau's discretion. "Nasa pamumuno na po nila iyan. Kung ano po ang nakikita nilang nararapat, as long na ang mga akusado ay nasa kustodiya po nila, nasa kanilang kamay na po ang pagpapasiya niyan," she stated. CANCELLED PGH VISIT Marcos was scheduled to have a visit to the Philippine General Hospital on Monday, September 14 but was cancelled Sunday night. Pressed why, Castro cited conflict in schedule with Marcos Jr. coming home from his participation in the recently concluded 18th BRICS Summit in India early Monday morning. "Kagagaling lang po kasi kagabi, madaling araw po dumating ang Pangulo. Alam ninyo naman po na halos mag-aalas singko na po dumating ang Pangulo. Hindi po naipagbigay—nabigay pabatid or nabigyan tayo ng kaalaman tungkol sa anong oras supposed to be kung pupunta man siya sa PGH, kasi kagagaling lang po niya sa India, kakatapos lang po ng kanyang trabaho at halos mag-aalas singko na po ng madaling araw dumating ang Pangulo," she said. The Palace official also denied that it had something to do with Romualdez who was then confined in the facility for an independent medical examination as ordered by the Sandiganbayan Third Division. "Wala. Walang napag-usapan patungkol diyan na iyon ang magiging dahilan. Nagkataon lang po siguro na kararating lang ng Pangulo, ng halos mag-aalas singko na po ng madaling araw, wala pa pong tulog iyon halos," she said. RELATED VIDEO:
